paper_title: Rethinking the Role of Prompting Strategies in LLM Test-Time Scaling A   Perspective of Probability Theory
caption: Results of combining adaptively scaling and dynamically choosing the optimal i on GPT-4o-mini on MATH.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The graph illustrates the relationship between sampling time and accuracy, comparing the performance of different prompting strategies. The x-axis, labeled "Sampling Time," has a linear scale and ranges from 0 to 25, with labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," also has a linear scale and spans from 66 to 87, with labels at intervals of 3.

The graph features six distinct lines, each representing a different prompting strategy or combination thereof. The lines are differentiated by color and marker style. 
The purple line with diamond markers represents "DiP" and starts at approximately 72 on the y-axis at a sampling time of 1, then increases to around 78 at a sampling time of 12, after which it plateaus. 
The orange line with square markers, representing "AnP," begins at about 66 and rises to roughly 72 at a sampling time of 4, before stabilizing. 
The blue line with triangle markers, labeled "CoT," commences at approximately 72 and ascends to around 78 at a sampling time of 12, then levels off. 
The cyan line with cross markers, representing "L2M," starts at about 70 and reaches around 77 at a sampling time of 12, after which it remains relatively stable. 
The peach line with asterisk markers, denoting "SBP," begins at approximately 72 and climbs to roughly 77 at a sampling time of 8, before plateauing with slight fluctuations. 
The black dashed line with square markers, representing "Dynamic w/ Oracle," starts at around 84 and gradually decreases to approximately 84 at a sampling time of 25. 
The red dashed line with circle markers, labeled "Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle," begins at about 85 and increases to roughly 87 at a sampling time of 6, then remains relatively stable.

Overall, the graph provides a visual comparison of how different prompting strategies perform in terms of accuracy as sampling time varies, highlighting their relative strengths and weaknesses.
model_annotations.German: The chart displays the accuracy of various prompting strategies over different sampling times. The x-axis represents the sampling time, ranging from 0 to 25 in increments of 5, with a linear scale. The y-axis represents accuracy, ranging from 66 to 87 in increments of 3, also with a linear scale. The chart compares six different lines, each representing a distinct prompting strategy: DiP (purple diamonds, solid line), AnP (orange squares, solid line), CoT (blue triangles, solid line), Dynamic w/ Oracle (black squares, dashed line), L2M (cyan triangles, solid line), and Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle (red circles, dashed line), and SBP (peach triangles, solid line). DiP starts at an accuracy of around 72 at a sampling time of 1, rising to approximately 78.5 at a sampling time of 12, before stabilizing around 78. AnP begins at about 72.5 and increases to roughly 73 at a sampling time of 8, then gradually declines to around 72.5 at a sampling time of 25. CoT starts at an accuracy of 72, rises to about 78 at a sampling time of 8, and stabilizes around 78. L2M begins at 74 and peaks at around 77.5 at a sampling time of 8, followed by a slight decline to approximately 76.5. SBP starts at about 75, dips at a sampling time of 4, and peaks at roughly 77.5 at a sampling time of 12, before falling back to around 77. Dynamic w/ Oracle begins at 84.5, rising to 85, then declining gradually to around 84. Adaptive + Dynamic w/ Oracle starts at 85, rises to roughly 87 at a sampling time of 4, and remains stable at 87.
